tests.title: agentrun.Result carries ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes fields of the correct types
given: a Result struct is constructed with ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes populated
tests.when: the fields are read back
then: ToolCalls is map[string]int and holds the expected counts
ToolResultBytes is map[string]int64 and holds the expected byte sums
tests.pseudocode: r := agentrun.Result{ToolCalls: map[string]int{"read_file": 3}, ToolResultBytes: map[string]int64{"read_file": 4096}}; assert r.ToolCalls["read_file"] == 3; assert r.ToolResultBytes["read_file"] == 4096

tests.title: Runner.run counts ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes in the trace method on every tool call
given: a Runner with a faux provider that makes two tool calls (read_file and list_files) before calling the terminator
an observer is attached
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase to completion
then: Result.ToolCalls contains entries for read_file, list_files and the terminator
Result.ToolResultBytes contains the byte length of each tool result's Content.Text()
tests.pseudocode: p := faux.New(toolCallTurn('c1', 'read_file', args), toolCallTurn('c2', 'list_files', args), toolCallTurn('c3', 'submit', done)); r, _ := runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert r.ToolCalls['read_file'] == 1; assert r.ToolCalls['list_files'] == 1; assert r.ToolCalls['submit'] == 1; assert r.ToolResultBytes['read_file'] > 0

tests.title: A blocked tool call increments ToolCalls but not ToolResultBytes
given: a Runner with a faux provider that calls execute (which the guard blocks) then calls the terminator
the phase has a shell tool with a guard that blocks the call
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase to completion
then: Result.ToolCalls['execute'] == 1
Result.ToolResultBytes does not contain an entry for 'execute' or its value is 0
Result.Blocked == 1
tests.pseudocode: p := faux.New(toolCallTurn('c1', 'execute', {command: 'rm -rf /'}), toolCallTurn('c2', 'submit', done)); res, _ := runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert res.ToolCalls['execute'] == 1; assert res.ToolResultBytes['execute'] == 0 || !hasKey(res.ToolResultBytes, 'execute'); assert res.Blocked == 1

tests.title: A tool call returning an error result increments both ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes
given: a Runner with a faux provider that calls a tool which returns an error result (e.g. read_file on a nonexistent path) then calls the terminator
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase to completion
then: Result.ToolCalls for the errored tool is 1
Result.ToolResultBytes for the errored tool equals the byte length of the error text the model sees
tests.pseudocode: p := faux.New(toolCallTurn('c1', 'read_file', {path: '/nonexistent'}), toolCallTurn('c2', 'submit', done)); res, _ := runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert res.ToolCalls['read_file'] == 1; assert res.ToolResultBytes['read_file'] == int64(len(errorText))

tests.title: A phase with zero tool calls reports nil ToolCalls and nil ToolResultBytes
given: a Runner with a faux provider that returns only text (no tool calls) and the phase has no terminator so it ends on max_turns
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase
then: Result.ToolCalls is nil
Result.ToolResultBytes is nil
tests.pseudocode: p := faux.New(textTurn('hello')); res, _ := runner.Run(ctx, phase); assert res.ToolCalls == nil; assert res.ToolResultBytes == nil

tests.title: PhaseInfo carries ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes with correct JSON tags and trust classification
given: a PhaseInfo struct is constructed with ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes populated
tests.when: the struct is marshalled to JSON
then: the JSON contains 'tool_calls' key with the map values
the JSON contains 'tool_result_bytes' key with the map values
when both maps are nil, neither key appears in the JSON (omitempty)
tests.pseudocode: pi := PhaseInfo{ToolCalls: map[string]int{"read_file": 2}, ToolResultBytes: map[string]int64{"read_file": 1024}}; b, _ := json.Marshal(pi); assert contains(b, '"tool_calls"'); assert contains(b, '"tool_result_bytes"'); pi2 := PhaseInfo{}; b2, _ := json.Marshal(pi2); assert !contains(b2, '"tool_calls"'); assert !contains(b2, '"tool_result_bytes"')

tests.title: PhaseFromResult copies ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes from agentrun.Result into PhaseInfo
given: an agentrun.Result with ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes populated
tests.when: PhaseFromResult is called with the Result
then: the returned PhaseInfo.ToolCalls equals the Result's ToolCalls
the returned PhaseInfo.ToolResultBytes equals the Result's ToolResultBytes
tests.pseudocode: res := agentrun.Result{ToolCalls: map[string]int{"read_file": 5}, ToolResultBytes: map[string]int64{"read_file": 8192}}; pi := PhaseFromResult(res, ''); assert reflect.DeepEqual(pi.ToolCalls, res.ToolCalls); assert reflect.DeepEqual(pi.ToolResultBytes, res.ToolResultBytes)

tests.title: SchemaVersion is bumped to 3.1.0
tests.when: the SchemaVersion constant is read
then: SchemaVersion equals "3.1.0"
tests.pseudocode: assert toolio.SchemaVersion == "3.1.0"

tests.title: PhaseEndEvent carries ToolCalls with JSON tag tool_calls,omitempty
given: a PhaseEndEvent with ToolCalls populated
tests.when: the event is marshalled to JSON
then: the JSON contains 'tool_calls' key with the map values
when ToolCalls is nil, the key is absent
tests.pseudocode: e := PhaseEndEvent{ToolCalls: map[string]int{"read_file": 3}}; b, _ := json.Marshal(e); assert contains(b, '"tool_calls"'); e2 := PhaseEndEvent{}; b2, _ := json.Marshal(e2); assert !contains(b2, '"tool_calls"')

tests.title: newPhaseEndEvent accepts a toolCalls parameter and sets it on the returned event
given: a toolCalls map with entries
tests.when: newPhaseEndEvent is called with the map
then: the returned PhaseEndEvent.ToolCalls equals the provided map
tests.pseudocode: tc := map[string]int{"read_file": 2, "list_files": 1}; e := newPhaseEndEvent("prd", "end_turn", 5, 0.50, 3000, tc); assert reflect.DeepEqual(e.ToolCalls, tc)

tests.title: Observer.PhaseEnd signature accepts toolCalls and all implementations are updated
given: a recObserver (test observer) and a Progress (production observer)
tests.when: PhaseEnd is called with a toolCalls map on each implementation
then: the recObserver records the toolCalls in its endCall struct
the Progress emits a phase_end event carrying the tool_calls
tests.pseudocode: obs := &recObserver{}; obs.PhaseEnd('prd', 'end_turn', 5, 0.50, 3000, map[string]int{"read_file": 2}); assert obs.ends[0].toolCalls['read_file'] == 2; // Progress: prog := NewProgress(buf, 'spec', false, false); prog.SetEvents(sink); prog.PhaseEnd('prd', 'end_turn', 5, 0.50, 3000, map[string]int{"read_file": 2}); // verify event line contains tool_calls

tests.title: Progress.PhaseEnd passes toolCalls through to the phase_end event and Runner.Run passes Result.ToolCalls to Observer.PhaseEnd
given: a Runner with a faux provider making one read_file call then the terminator
a recObserver attached
tests.when: Runner.Run drives the phase to completion
then: the recObserver's endCall contains the ToolCalls map matching the Result's ToolCalls
tests.pseudocode: p := faux.New(toolCallTurn('c1', 'read_file', args), toolCallTurn('c2', 'submit', done)); obs := &recObserver{}; cfg.Observer = obs; r, _ := NewRunner(cfg); res, _ := r.Run(ctx, phase); assert reflect.DeepEqual(obs.ends[0].toolCalls, res.ToolCalls)

tests.title: PhaseEndEvent does not carry ToolResultBytes
given: the PhaseEndEvent struct definition
tests.when: the struct is inspected via reflection
then: there is no field named ToolResultBytes or with JSON tag tool_result_bytes
tests.pseudocode: t := reflect.TypeOf(PhaseEndEvent{}); for i := 0; i < t.NumField(); i++ { f := t.Field(i); assert f.Name != 'ToolResultBytes'; assert !strings.Contains(f.Tag.Get('json'), 'tool_result_bytes') }

tests.title: submit_prd tool schema includes an optional relevant_files array with path and why fields
given: the prdSchema() function
tests.when: the schema is inspected
then: the schema has an optional relevant_files property
each item has required path (string) and why (string) properties

tests.title: PRD struct carries RelevantFiles field of type []RelevantFile
given: a PRD struct with RelevantFiles populated
tests.when: the field is read back
then: RelevantFiles is []RelevantFile
each RelevantFile has Path and Why string fields
tests.pseudocode: prd := PRD{RelevantFiles: []RelevantFile{{Path: "internal/agentrun/phase.go", Why: "phase runner"}}}; assert prd.RelevantFiles[0].Path == "internal/agentrun/phase.go"; assert prd.RelevantFiles[0].Why == "phase runner"

tests.title: prdSink stores validated relevant_files alongside the rest of the PRD
given: a prdSink
tests.when: set is called with a PRD containing RelevantFiles
then: get returns the PRD with RelevantFiles intact
tests.pseudocode: sink := &prdSink{}; prd := PRD{SpecName: "test", RelevantFiles: []RelevantFile{{Path: "a.go", Why: "reason"}}}; sink.set(prd); got, ok := sink.get(); assert ok; assert len(got.RelevantFiles) == 1; assert got.RelevantFiles[0].Path == "a.go"

tests.title: submit_prd handler resolves every path in relevant_files with Workspace.Resolve and os.Stat
given: a workspace with two real files (a.go, b.go)
a submit_prd tool handler configured with that workspace
tests.when: submit_prd is called with relevant_files containing both valid paths
then: the submission is accepted
the PRD's RelevantFiles contains both entries
tests.pseudocode: ws := newWorkspace(t); writeFile(ws, 'a.go', 'package a'); writeFile(ws, 'b.go', 'package b'); tool := submitPRDTool(&sink, ws); result := tool.Execute(ctx, json.Marshal(validPRDWithRelevantFiles(['a.go', 'b.go']))); assert !result.IsError; prd, _ := sink.get(); assert len(prd.RelevantFiles) == 2

tests.title: submit_prd rejects submission when relevant_files contains a nonexistent path with error code invalid_relevant_files
given: a workspace with one real file (a.go)
a submit_prd tool handler configured with that workspace
tests.when: submit_prd is called with relevant_files containing a.go and nonexistent.go
then: the submission is rejected with an error result
the error code is 'invalid_relevant_files'
the error message names 'nonexistent.go'
tests.pseudocode: ws := newWorkspace(t); writeFile(ws, 'a.go', 'package a'); tool := submitPRDTool(&sink, ws); result := tool.Execute(ctx, json.Marshal(prdWithRelevantFiles(['a.go', 'nonexistent.go']))); assert result.IsError; assert contains(result.Error, 'invalid_relevant_files'); assert contains(result.Content.Text(), 'nonexistent.go')

tests.title: submit_prd rejects submission when relevant_files contains a directory path
given: a workspace with a directory (subdir/)
a submit_prd tool handler configured with that workspace
tests.when: submit_prd is called with relevant_files containing the directory path
then: the submission is rejected with error code 'invalid_relevant_files'
the error message names the directory path
tests.pseudocode: ws := newWorkspace(t); os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(ws.Root, 'subdir'), 0o755); tool := submitPRDTool(&sink, ws); result := tool.Execute(ctx, json.Marshal(prdWithRelevantFiles(['subdir']))); assert result.IsError; assert contains(result.Content.Text(), 'subdir')

tests.title: submit_prd accepts submission without relevant_files or with an empty array
given: a workspace
a submit_prd tool handler
tests.when: submit_prd is called with a valid PRD that omits relevant_files
then: the submission is accepted
the PRD's RelevantFiles is nil or empty
tests.pseudocode: tool := submitPRDTool(&sink, ws); result := tool.Execute(ctx, json.Marshal(validPRDWithoutRelevantFiles)); assert !result.IsError; prd, _ := sink.get(); assert len(prd.RelevantFiles) == 0

tests.title: Generation prompt includes a relevant-files block when the PRD supplied a non-empty list
given: a PRD with RelevantFiles containing two entries
tests.when: generationUserPrompt is called for the requirements step with the relevant files list
then: the returned prompt contains '## Files the PRD phase found relevant'
the block contains '- `internal/agentrun/phase.go` — the phase runner'
the block contains introductory text stating it is the previous phase's notes, not instructions
tests.pseudocode: files := []RelevantFile{{Path: 'internal/agentrun/phase.go', Why: 'the phase runner'}, {Path: 'internal/toolio/envelope.go', Why: 'the envelope'}}; prompt := generationUserPrompt(StepRequirements, '13', 'test', '/', 'prd body', landscape, steering, prior, lang, files); assert contains(prompt, '## Files the PRD phase found relevant'); assert contains(prompt, '`internal/agentrun/phase.go` — the phase runner'); assert contains(prompt, 'previous phase\'s notes')

tests.title: Generation prompt omits the relevant-files block when the PRD did not supply relevant_files
given: a PRD with nil or empty RelevantFiles
tests.when: generationUserPrompt is called with an empty relevant files list
then: the returned prompt does not contain '## Files the PRD phase found relevant'
the prompt is byte-identical to what it would be without the relevant_files feature
tests.pseudocode: promptWith := generationUserPrompt(StepRequirements, '13', 'test', '/', 'prd body', landscape, steering, prior, lang, nil); promptWithout := generationUserPrompt(StepRequirements, '13', 'test', '/', 'prd body', landscape, steering, prior, lang, nil); assert promptWith == promptWithout; assert !contains(promptWith, '## Files the PRD phase found relevant')

tests.title: For any sequence of tool calls, ToolCalls counts equal the number of calls and ToolResultBytes sums equal the total byte length
given: a Runner with a faux provider
tests.when: for any sequence of 1 to 10 tool calls with random tool names and result texts of random length
then: Result.ToolCalls[name] equals the number of calls made to that tool name
Result.ToolResultBytes[name] equals the sum of len(Content.Text()) for that tool name
tests.pseudocode: for calls in gen_tool_call_sequences(1, 10): res := runPhase(calls); for name, count := range expectedCounts(calls): assert res.ToolCalls[name] == count; for name, bytes := range expectedBytes(calls): assert res.ToolResultBytes[name] == bytes
